idiom_name: higher-order wrapper function / Express middleware chain
implementation_notes: In JavaScript the interceptor is a function that returns a function: wrap the audited service method or route handler, record the invocation, await the target, record the outcome and rethrow failure - Express's app.use((req, res, next) => ...) chain is the same realization for requests, with next() playing the role of proceed(). It is the default because it costs nothing, works in every runtime, and keeps the audit logic next to the operation it wraps; its limit is that only the wrapped function is covered.
pitfalls: `this` is lost when a method is passed around: bind the target or apply it explicitly.
Forgetting to await the target records a success before the call resolves.
Express error handling depends on the chain: a wrapper that calls next() instead of next(err), or swallows the rejection, removes the failure record and changes the response path.

variants.name: ES2015 Proxy with get/apply traps
variants.idiom_name: new Proxy(target, handler) intercepting property lookups
variants.implementation_notes: new Proxy(target, handler) intercepts operations on the object itself: a get trap can return an audited wrapper around any function property, so one interceptor covers an entire service object without enumerating its methods, and the handler object takes the place of the interceptor class. Choose it when the interception point is object access rather than specific calls; the costs are a language floor (ES2015), changed identity for the wrapped object, and trap invariants that can make code throw where a plain wrapper would not.
pitfalls: Use Reflect.get(obj, prop, recv) inside the trap: reading obj[prop] directly breaks prototype chains, getters and private fields on the receiver.
Each trapped function is a fresh closure, so identity checks (===) against the original methods fail and proxies must not be recreated per call.
Proxy invariants for non-configurable, non-writable properties can make traps throw where a plain wrapper function would have worked.
